Performers
Dietrich Fischer-⁠Dieskau (baritone), Berlin Philharmonic (orchestra), Rudolf Kempe (conductor) Documented

The Commons description identifies all three performing credits; the independent catalogue corroborates the pairing.

[1] [5]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The source identifies the orchestral song, but not its performing edition or editorial alterations. The listening notes use the low-voice orchestral score, C. F. Kahnt plate 4460, for passage-level scoring; they do not claim this exact printed edition was on the performers’ desks.

[1] [2]
Recorded
20–⁠21 June 1955 Documented

Commons and the Naxos reissue back cover give 20–⁠21 June 1955. The two-day span is for the cycle’s sessions; the movement is not assigned to a particular day.

[1] [5]
Place
Jesus-⁠Christus-⁠Kirche, Berlin Documented

The Naxos back cover identifies Jesus-⁠Christus-⁠Kirche in Berlin for these sessions; this is session evidence, not evidence that the Commons transfer comes from that reissue.

[5]
Label
EMI Documented

Commons names its source as “CD audio EMI”. This is the identified CD source label, not an assertion about the original session medium.

[1]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

No catalogue number identifying the CD used for the Commons upload is supplied. Naxos 8.111300 documents the same recording sessions, but is a different reissue: its catalogue number and Mark Obert-⁠Thorn restoration credit are not attributed to the unidentified EMI CD.

[1] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

No matrix, take or original side identification is supplied. The absence of those details is not treated as proof that no historical identifiers exist.

[1]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The Commons uploader is not treated as a transfer or mastering engineer. No such credit for this particular CD-to-Ogg transfer is identified.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is supplied; upload dates and historical recording dates are not substituted for it.

[1]
Processing
Commons provides an uploaded Ogg Vorbis file and an MP3 access derivative. Documented

The embedded Ogg encoder is Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20100325 (Everywhere). The original session medium, earlier mastering, noise reduction and editing history are unestablished.

[1]
Composition rights
The Sibley Music Library marks its early printed orchestral score, including Rückert’s text, as public domain. Documented

The catalogue gives Mahler’s dates as 1860–⁠1911 and Rückert’s as 1788–⁠1866. This refers to the historical composition and text, not an unidentified modern performing edition; the catalogue’s inconsistent publication year is not adopted.

[2]
Recording rights
Territorial — Commons applies PD-EU-audio to the sound recording. Documented

The template concerns the rights of performers and phonogram producers, not merely the composition. The recording is accepted on that EU territorial basis. United States status and worldwide clearance are not established; no US pre-1926 claim is made.

[1] [4]

Gustav Mahler, Kindertotenlieder, V. In diesem Wetter, in diesem Braus; Dietrich Fischer-⁠Dieskau, baritone; Berlin Philharmonic; Rudolf Kempe, conductor. Recorded 20–⁠21 June 1955. EMI CD source via Wikimedia Commons; Commons states PD-EU-audio (EU territorial status; US status unestablished). Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — Mahler - Kindertotenlieder, V (Fischer-⁠Dieskau, Kempe, 1955).ogg — File description: performers, recording date, CD source and PD-EU-audio licensing template; embedded Metadata and Transcode status. The named revision freezes the provenance claim.. Accessed 2026-10-16.
  2. Sibley Music Library — Kindertotenlieder, C. F. Kahnt plate 4460 — Full-score catalogue: five song titles, composer and poet dates, publisher and plate, 86-page miniature orchestral score; “This item is in the public domain.” The catalogue’s 1900 date predates completion and is not used.. Accessed 2026-10-16.
  3. Paul Banks — Kindertotenlieder work catalogue — Composition chronology, versions, original keys, scoring, first performance and publication history.. Accessed 2026-10-16.
  4. Wikimedia Commons — PD-EU-audio template — Licensing text: expiry of performers’ and producers’ sound-recording rights in the EU; not a substitute for composition copyright.. Accessed 2026-10-16.
  5. Naxos Historical 8.111300 — reissue back cover — Tracks 5–⁠9: Fischer-⁠Dieskau, Berlin Philharmonic, Rudolf Kempe; recorded 20–⁠21 June 1955 at Jesus-⁠Christus-⁠Kirche, Berlin. Reissue production and restoration credits belong to Naxos, not the Commons source.. Accessed 2026-10-16.
